themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 4 this week versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors, enforcement gaps, or new resident complaints about street vending in Bushwick this week.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
Spike is acute and concentrated in the most recent reporting period
No prior pattern of mobile food vendor complaints in 90-day historical data
reporting_angles: Map locations of this week's complaints and interview residents about which vendors are appearing; check if vendors are licensed
Contact Department of Health to ask if there's been a shift in enforcement or vendor activity permits in Bushwick this week

themes_detail.label: Park Rule Violations & Animal Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Park-related violations spiked dramatically: park rule violations jumped to 3 last week (2300% above baseline of 0.1/week, z-score: 8.69) and animal-in-park complaints hit 4 last week (540% above 0.6/week baseline, z-score: 4.85), plus 4 noise-park complaints this week—signaling a sudden shift in park use or enforcement over the past 1-2 weeks.
evidence: Park rule violations: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Animal-in-park complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 4.85)
Noise-park complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 4.85)
Convergence of three park-related complaint types within 1-2 weeks suggests a focal problem
reporting_angles: Investigate Bushwick Inlet Park (referenced in recent Hell Gate article about unfinished development)—are construction activities disrupting park use or attracting off-leash dogs?
Interview Parks Department and local precinct about what sparked the uptick in rule violations and animal complaints

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged to 3 this week versus 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting recent unauthorized tree cutting, removal, or damage in Bushwick affecting multiple locations.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
No prior clustering of tree damage complaints in 90-day baseline data
Aligns with community board budget requests for green infrastructure and property evaluation (DEP)
reporting_angles: Map the three tree damage complaints to identify if they cluster geographically or if they point to a single contractor or development project
Check DOB permits and ULURP applications (150 Noll, 460 Troutman, 132 Melrose rezoning) to see if recent construction is driving tree removals

themes_detail.label: Water System Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints peaked at 93 two weeks ago versus an 8-week baseline of 18.0 per week—a 417% increase (z-score: 9.25)—indicating a significant water infrastructure or service issue that affected residents 1-2 weeks ago.
evidence: 93 water system complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 18.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (417% spike, z-score: 9.25)
Spike is past-facing (2 weeks ago); unclear if issue is ongoing or resolved
No current supporting data on whether water system remains compromised
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine what caused the spike 2 weeks ago—was it a main break, treatment issue, or widespread service outage?
Investigate whether residents are still experiencing water problems or if the issue has been resolved; interview affected buildings

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping & Sanitation Gap
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints jumped to 7 last week versus 1.0 per week baseline (600% spike, z-score: 4.54), and 'unsanitary condition' and 'dirty condition' complaints remain in top 10 issues (499 and 444 complaints over 90 days), suggesting ongoing neglect of street cleanliness that may have visibly worsened over the past 1-2 weeks.
evidence: Street sweeping complaints: 7 last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (600% spike, z-score: 4.54)
Unsanitary condition complaints: 499 over 90 days (persistent volume issue)
Dirty condition complaints: 444 over 90 days (persistent volume issue)
Community board repeatedly requests other capital budget for DSNY, indicating chronic sanitation infrastructure concern
reporting_angles: Walk streets flagged in the 7 complaints last week and document current cleanliness; photograph before/after if possible
Interview DSNY about staffing levels, equipment availability, and street sweeping schedules in Bushwick; check if there have been recent service cuts or route changes
